key_insight: Preoperative fasting glucose showed a U-shaped association with postoperative delirium, with the lowest observed risk between >5.92 and ≤9.75 mmol/L.
clinical_relevance: Preoperative glucose may help identify older adults with diabetes at higher delirium risk, but these observational findings do not establish treatment targets.
method: Multicentre retrospective cohort of 2,157 older adults with diabetes undergoing non-cardiac surgery at 20 Chinese hospitals.
Delirium assessed prospectively using 3D-CAM within 7 postoperative days.
Cox models with restricted cubic splines assessed associations; machine learning–guided cut-point analysis evaluated thresholds.
evidence_signal: Delirium occurred in 13.3%, 9.7%, and 18.5% of the lower, middle, and higher glucose groups, respectively; the nonlinear association was significant (P=0.03).
watch_item: Observational, data-derived thresholds require external validation and do not show that changing glucose levels prevents delirium.
paper_title: U-Shaped Association Between Preoperative Fasting Blood Glucose and Postoperative Delirium in Elderly Diabetic Patients: A Multicentre Retrospective Cohort Study
